chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abdullah who said: We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he asked us: Is there among you anyone who has the knowledge of my uncle Zayd ibn Ali?

So a man from the group said: I have knowledge from the knowledge of your uncle. We were with him one night in the house of Muawiya ibn Ishaq al-Ansari when he said: Come, let us go pray in Masjid al-Sahla. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And did he? He said: No, a matter came up that preoccupied him from going.

So he (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, if he sought refuge with Allah through it for a year, He would have sheltered him. Do you not know that it is the place of the house of the Prophet Idris (peace be upon him), and in which he used to sew? And from it Ibrahim (peace be upon him) marched to Yemen with the Amaliqa, and from it Dawud (peace be upon him) marched against Jalut.

And indeed in it is a green stone, in which is the likeness of every Prophet, and from beneath that very stone the clay of every Prophet was taken, and it is the resting place of the Rider. It was said: And who is the Rider? He (peace be upon him) said: Al-Khizr (peace be upon him).

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ السَّهْلَةِ: Masjid al-Sahla (The Mosque of the Plain)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and historical virtues of Masjid al-Sahla according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual lineage of Masjid al-Sahla, identifying it as the dwelling of Prophet Idris and the departure point for Ibrahim’s campaign against the Amalekites and Dawud’s march against Jalut. The text highlights a unique metaphysical element—a green stone bearing the likeness of every Prophet, from which the clay of each Prophet was taken—underscoring the site's role as a resting place for Al-Khizr, a figure of enduring divine guidance in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Abu Dawood, from Abdullah Bin Aban who said, 
‘We went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> asked us: ‘Is there anyone among you who has knowledge with him of my<sup>asws</sup> uncle Ziyad Bin Ali?’

So a man from the group said, ‘I do. With me is knowledge from the knowledge of yourasws uncle. We were with him one night by the door of Muawiya Bin Is’haq Al-Ansary when he said, ‘Come with me so that we pray Salāt in Masjid Al-Sahla’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘And did he?’ So he said, ‘No. A matter came up, so it pre-occupied him from the going’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Had he sought refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with it for a year, He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Sheltered him. But, do you not know that it is the place of the house of Idrees<sup>as</sup> the Prophet<sup>as</sup>, and in which he<sup>as</sup> used to sew? And from it did Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> go to Al-Yemen with Al-Amaaliqa, and from it did Dawood<sup>as</sup> go against Goliath;

and that in it is the green stone in which is a resemblance of every Prophet<sup>as</sup>; and it is from beneath that very stone the clay of every Prophet<sup>as</sup> was taken, and it is a disembarkation of the rider’. It was said, ‘And who is the rider?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Al-Khizr<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn abu Dawud from ‘Abd Allah ibn Aban who has said the following: “Once, we visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he asked us, ‘Does anyone of you have anything of the knowledge of my uncle, Zayd ibn Ali?’

A man from the group said, ‘I have something of the knowledge of your uncle. Once, we were in the presence of Imam one night in the house of Mu‘awiyah ibn Ishaq al-Ansariy when he said, “Allow us to visit al-Sahlah Masjid to perform Salah (prayer).’” Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then asked, ‘Did he do so?’ He (the man) replied, ‘Something came up that prevented him from visiting al-Sahlah Masjid.’

The Imam then said, ‘By Allah, had he sought refuge with Allah therein for a year he would have given him such refuge. You should take notice that it is the house of prophet Idris. Therein he did his sewing works. From this place Ibrahim started his journey to Yemen, where al-‘Amaliqah people has settled down. Dawud began his move against Jalut (Goliath) from this place.

In it, there is the green stone on which every prophet’s picture exists. From under this stone the clay of every prophet was taken and it is the place where the rider disembarks for rest.’ It was asked, ‘Who is the rider?’ The Imam replied, ‘He is al- Khadir.’”
